newsitem.title: UK: Israel Eurobond expected after London presentation.
newsitem.headline: Israel Eurobond expected after London presentation.

text.p: Israel will woo potential investors in London later this week ahead of the launch of its long-planned debut Eurobond, dealers said on Tuesday.
Minister of economic affairs Shlomo Maoz and finance ministry director general David Brodett are likely to attend the presentations in London on Wednesday.
The Eurobond will be a benchmark for other Israeli borrowers. In May, Maoz said: "We don't need the money but want to establish a benchmark so borrowers from the business sector can raise funds."
Israel has said it wants to raise $200-$300 million at five- or 10-year maturity following investor presentations in Frankfurt, Tokyo and London.
Merrill lynch was awarded the mandate in May this year to lead manage the transaction.
The bond will be the first to be issued under Israel's $750 million Euro medium-term note programme and the second Israeli offering without the backing of U.S. loan guarantees.
Standard & Poor's rated the issue A- on Monday. Israel is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
"The outlook on the rating is stable," S&P said, adding despite setbacks in the peace process, Israel had a secure geopolitical position.

Despite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's comments over the weekend -- that the Jordan Valley area of the occupied West Bank would be a part of Israel forever -- S&P said external security risks were largely offset by strong diplomatic and financial support from the U.S.
S&P said the high stakes for all sides in the Middle East should ensure progress on the peace process resumed.
